events.title: Edward the Confessor's Westminster Abbey is consecrated
events.description: Edward the Confessor's new abbey church at Westminster was consecrated, though the king was too ill to attend and died a week later. Every crowned English monarch since 1066 has been crowned there.

events.title: Galileo observes Neptune without realising it
events.description: While observing Jupiter, Galileo recorded a faint 'star' that was in fact Neptune. He did not recognise it as a planet, and its formal discovery came only in 1846.

events.title: John C. Calhoun becomes the first US vice-president to resign
events.description: John C. Calhoun resigned the vice-presidency to take a Senate seat, where he could better defend South Carolina during the Nullification Crisis. He had served under both John Quincy Adams and Andrew Jackson.

events.title: The Lumière brothers hold the first paid public film screening
events.description: At the Grand Café in Paris, Auguste and Louis Lumière projected ten short films to a paying audience. The screening is often taken as the birth of cinema.

events.title: An earthquake and tsunami destroy Messina
events.description: A powerful earthquake and tsunami struck the Strait of Messina, destroying Messina in Sicily and Reggio Calabria. Around 75,000 to 80,000 people died, making it Europe's deadliest recorded earthquake.
